thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate and latency on embeddings-batch endpoint (/v1/embeddings/batch). 5xxs spiking to 12%, p95 latency from 1.2s -> 5s, sustained for ~3m. svc-monitor
pagerduty: Paging Maya (oncall) and Joel (eng-sre). Severity: P1
Maya (oncall): on it, looking at dashboards now. correlation with increased traffic from a handful of IP ranges?
Joel (eng-sre): I'm seeing a fanout pattern — many small requests to the batch endpoint with 1-2 vector items each. Throughput up x6, KCACHE miss rate up. Likely scraper.
Maya (oncall): good call. any UA or header fingerprint?
Sam (eng-infra): raw ingress logs show repeated UA strings like "python-requests/2.31" and some custom bot UAs. src CIDRs: 207.46.0.0/16 & 45.77.120.0/22 (suspicious). Snapshot:
```
GET /v1/embeddings/batch 200 0.35ms "python-requests/2.31" 45.77.121.12
POST /v1/embeddings/batch 502 10ms "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0)" 207.46.12.9
```
Lucy (security): likely coordinated scraper fleet. Recommend temporary WAF rule to block UA patterns + CIDR block, and tighten per-token quotas for anonymous tier.
Maya (oncall): propose immediate mitigations: 1) disable /v1/embeddings/batch public access (keep non-batch endpoints) 2) apply rate-limit 10r/s per IP for embeddings endpoints 3) add WAF rule for known bot UA regex and the two CIDRs 4) increase token-cost accounting so heavy clients hit quota sooner
Joel (eng-sre): I can push the rate-limit and quota-slice in edge-gateway now. Will also enable adaptive backpressure so long-running requests drop to best-effort.
Sam (eng-infra): disabling batch endpoint via feature-flag now -> rolled, edge returning 410 for batch requests from anonymous clients. Confirmed: calls dropped ~75% in last 30s.
Maya (oncall): WAF rule applied for UA regex /python-requests|bingbot|scraper-fleet/i and CIDRs blocked at edge -> seeing immediate reduction in bad traffic. Error rate coming down to 4%.
Nina (support): heads up - I'll draft a short customer notice for customers on anon plans: "We detected abusive traffic to embeddings batch endpoints; we’ve temporarily disabled public batch endpoint while we mitigate. Impact: batch requests will receive 410. Single-item embeddings unaffected." Want approval to post to status page?
Product Ops: please follow conservative wording. Also need list of potentially affected API keys/tenants.
Joel (eng-sre): extracting top API keys hitting the endpoint now. Preliminary: ~90% of volume from unauthenticated/anonymous traffic and 5 keys that look compromised. I'll DM details to Security & Support.
Lucy (security): I want fingerprints for the 5 keys. Recommend immediate rotation for those keys and throttling for their orgs.
Maya (oncall): handing off to night oncall (Joel) in 25m. Summary for handoff: mitigations applied = batch endpoint disabled for anonymous, edge rate-limit per IP 10r/s, WAF UA+CIDR block, flagged 5 suspicious API keys for rotation, monitoring alerting lowered but still watch. Returning dashboards link: https://dash.internal/redwood/embeddings
Joel (eng-sre): I'll own overnight. Next steps: keep WAF blocks for 2h, escalate to full CIDR blackhole if traffic rebounds, prepare rollback plan to re-enable batch with stricter quota profiles if false positive discovered.
Nina (support): status note ready, will post after brief review. Sent to Product Ops for sign-off.
Product Ops: approved copy. Post to status page and DM top customers that use embeddings batches.
Maya (oncall): closing active paging; if error rate spikes >8% re-open. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigation active, monitoring). If new spike occurs, paging will resume.
